classification.difficultyReason: Read explicitly labelled radii, square them, and select the positive or negative square root according to the semicircle's orientation.

inlines.text: Find the equations of the following.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, Q10; first diagram row, left.
spec.description: Unfilled full circle centred at the axes intersection, with both positive intercepts labelled 5. Positive axis arrowheads and x/y labels are retained; there are no endpoint dots, grid lines or additional tick marks.
spec.mathematics: Centre (0,0), radius 5; equal physical x and y coordinate units.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens remain visible. The requested equation appears only in the answer.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, Q11; first diagram row, right.
spec.description: Unfilled full circle centred at the axes intersection. Both positive intercepts are labelled with the stacked fraction 1/3. Retain positive axis arrows and x/y labels, without additional tick marks.
spec.mathematics: Centre (0,0), radius 1/3; equal physical x and y coordinate units.
spec.answerVisibility: The two fractional radius labels are supplied givens; the equation is answer-only.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, Q12; second diagram row, left.
spec.description: Unfilled upper semicircular arc with horizontal endpoint labels −3 and 3 below the axis and a top label 3 above/left of the vertical axis. Retain both axes and positive arrows; no endpoint dots or extra ticks.
spec.mathematics: Centre (0,0), radius 3; endpoints (−3,0) and (3,0), maximum (0,3). Equal physical coordinate units.
spec.answerVisibility: The upper orientation and all three numerical labels are visible givens. No equation is printed in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The radius is $3$. Use the positive square root for the upper semicircle.

$$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{3^2-x^2}\\y&=\sqrt{9-x^2}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, Q13; second diagram row, right.
spec.description: Unfilled lower semicircular arc. Labels −√3 and √3 sit above the horizontal endpoints; −√3 sits below/left of the lowest point on the vertical axis. Retain both axes and positive arrows without endpoint dots or additional ticks.
spec.mathematics: Centre (0,0), radius √3; endpoints (−√3,0) and (√3,0), minimum (0,−√3). Equal physical coordinate units.
spec.answerVisibility: All source radical labels and the lower orientation are permanent givens; the requested equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The radius is $\sqrt{3}$. Use the negative square root for the lower semicircle.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2-x^2}\\y&=-\sqrt{3-x^2}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, Q14; third diagram row, left.
spec.description: Unfilled upper semicircular arc with stacked fractional endpoint labels −1/5 and 1/5 below the horizontal axis and a top label 1/5 above/left of the vertical axis. Retain positive axis arrows and x/y labels; no endpoint dots or extra ticks.
spec.mathematics: Centre (0,0), radius 1/5; endpoints (−1/5,0) and (1/5,0), maximum (0,1/5). Equal physical coordinate units.
spec.answerVisibility: The three fractional labels are visible givens. The equation and squared radius remain answer-only.

answer.worked:
The radius is $\frac{1}{5}$. Use the positive square root for the upper semicircle.

$$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2-x^2}\\y&=\sqrt{\frac{1}{25}-x^2}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, Q15; third diagram row, right.
spec.description: Unfilled lower semicircular arc with stacked fractional endpoint labels −3/2 and 3/2 above the horizontal axis and −3/2 below/left of the lowest point. Retain both axes, positive arrows and x/y labels, without endpoint dots or extra ticks.
spec.mathematics: Centre (0,0), radius 3/2; endpoints (−3/2,0) and (3/2,0), minimum (0,−3/2). Equal physical coordinate units.
spec.answerVisibility: All fractional labels and the lower-half orientation remain visible. The equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The radius is $\frac{3}{2}$. Use the negative square root for the lower semicircle.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2-x^2}\\y&=-\sqrt{\frac{9}{4}-x^2}\end{align*}$$
